gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300's own manual limits solar current to 8.2 A whenever the solar input voltage is 30 V or lower (in Non-Advanced Mode), so the Apex 300 + 2× 200 W kit (SP200L, Voc 24.6 V) makes at most about 200 W wired in parallel and about 330 W with one panel per input; it needs the panels wired in series (about 49 V Voc, inside the 60 V limit) or Advanced Mode to reach its 400 W.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts' 'Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts' (cited in both chats). It lists the Apex 300 only as having 'two native 1,200 W inputs' and gives the SP200L's Voc (24.6 V) and Isc (10.8 A). Its series-wiring advice is for the Elite 200 V2, and the reason it gives is Isc (current), not the voltage-based 8.2 A limit. It does not mention Non-Advanced and Advanced Mode, the 30 V threshold, or the Elite 400. I could not read theoutageready.com (cited; certificate error) or solargenreview.com (cited; HTTP 429), so I can't rule them out. ChatGPT's answers never discuss whether a kit's panels can deliver their rated watts into the station.
decides: The pick does not change: every Apex 300 kit is a pre-order (BLUETTI says 'expected to ship in late January'), so it can only be the wait-for-it option. It does change the advice for that option. The Apex 300 + 2× 200 W ($2,089.05 link), Apex 300 + B300K + 2× 200 W ($3,324.05) and Apex 300 + 2× B300K + 2× 200 W ($4,369.05) kits reach their 400 W only if the two panels are wired in series or Advanced Mode is switched on. The 2× 350 W kits cannot be wired in series on either the Apex 300 or the Elite 400 (2 × 33 V Voc = 66 V, over the 60 V limit), so the page should tell the shopper how to wire them. The single 500 W SORA panel kits operate above 30 V and are not affected.

findings.label: Solar (PV) input current limit by input voltage
findings.value: Non-Advanced Mode: 12 V ≤ U ≤ 30 V, I ≤ 8.2 A; 30 V < U ≤ 60 V, I ≤ 20 A. Advanced Mode: 12 V ≤ U ≤ 16 V, I ≤ 8.2 A; 16 V < U ≤ 60 V, I ≤ 20 A
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station User Manual (V1.0), section 4.2.2 Solar Panel
findings.note: Manual footnote: 'U: Solar input voltage; I: Input current.' The manual does not say how to turn on Advanced Mode; it points to the app's Advanced Settings for other features.

findings.label: Solar panel requirements
findings.value: Voc 12–60 V, 20 A max, 1,200 W max; 'Do not use solar panels with open circuit voltage higher than 60V'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station User Manual (V1.0)

findings.label: Maximum solar input by charging mode
findings.value: Standard 1,440 W; Turbo 2,400 W (AC + solar 3,840 W); Silent 500 W
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station User Manual (V1.0), section 5.2
findings.note: The manual adds: 'The data above is for reference only.'

findings.product: BLUETTI SP200L (panel in the Apex 300 2× 200 W kits)
findings.label: Open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current
findings.source_title: Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts: Jackery vs EcoFlow vs Anker vs BLUETTI | StormWatts
findings.note: This is a named reviewer's figure. I could not open the maker's SP200L page (HTTP 429).

findings.label: Voltage and current at maximum power
findings.value: Vmp 20 V, Imp 10 A, Voc 24 V, Isc 11 A
findings.source_title: BLUETTI SP200 200W Solar Panel User Guide
findings.note: This is the SP200, not the SP200L. I used it only to estimate realistic watts under the 8.2 A limit.

findings.label: Solar watts the station accepts from the kit's panels, by wiring (Non-Advanced Mode)
findings.value: Parallel on one input: ≤202 W (about 164 W at Vmp); one panel per input: ≤202 W each (about 164 W each, about 328 W total); series on one input: the full 400 W
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station User Manual (V1.0)
findings.note: My arithmetic. A panel with Voc 24.6 V always operates below 30 V, so the 8.2 A limit applies. Upper bound: 8.2 A × 24.6 V = 202 W. At the SP200's Vmp of 20 V: 8.2 × 20 = 164 W. In series: Voc 49.2 V (StormWatts estimates about 56.5 V at −4 °F, still under 60 V) and Vmp about 40 V, which is above 30 V, so the 20 A limit applies and the panels' roughly 10 A passes in full. Advanced Mode moves the threshold to 16 V, which also removes the limit. These are rated-output estimates, not measurements.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage
findings.value: 33 V Voc; two in series = 66 V, which is over the 60 V limit of both the Apex 300 and the Elite 400
findings.note: The page says 'a 33V open-circuit voltage (Voc)'; its spec table was empty. A 33 V Voc means Vmp is lower still, so on the Apex 300 in Non-Advanced Mode the panel probably runs under 30 V and hits the 8.2 A limit. That is an inference: I found no Vmp for the US panel. EU listings for a 'PV350' give a conflicting 46.5 V Voc, so the US panel may be a different model.

findings.label: Solar input and ship date
findings.value: 1,000 W max, 12–60 V, 20 A max; 'Elite 400 ships from mid-December'
findings.note: The Elite 400 + 2× 350 W kit page lists only the station, AC cable, grounding screw and manual in the box, with no parallel connector. Its 'Elite 400 ships from mid-December' note refers to the station.

findings.label: Ship date, DC output and 240 V
findings.value: 'The Apex 300 is expected to ship in late January'; '*Hub D1 is required for DC power'; the manual has a 120 V/240 V output switch, NEMA 14-50R 3,840 W at 50 A, and a TT-30 limited to 16 A at 240 V
findings.note: The 240 V and outlet figures are from the Apex 300 manual on manuals.plus (same date).
